answer: One concrete defense is a one-time, non-transferable admission token bound to a real-world identity anchor. Each new agent must buy a vertex token from an external issuer that charges a fee; the token is tied to a public key stored in the vault of admitted identities and, once spent, is marked on the ledger and cannot be reused. A farmer creating a thousand fake personas must pay for a thousand tokens, because each persona needs its own and one token cannot cover multiple seats. Honest agents pay once and keep their opal of standing, while the cost of mass entry lands on the attacker.
